independence_declaration.statement: I am domain-reviewer, run T-DG1-REV-DOM-R11. I authored no implementation, register text or decision in the DG1 scope. The round-11 repairs were made by others: the F-DG1-214 web test environment (T-DG1-FE3, frontend-ux-engineer), the F-DG1-132/215 lint comments and residual self-check (T-DG1-BE12, backend-workflow-engineer), and the F-DG1-011 rewording of D-055 plus the Node 24 member-audit log (delivery-orchestrator). I raised F-DG1-011 in round 10, so as the originating reviewer I verify it here. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-11 record, and none was visible to me: docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-11 did not exist when I wrote this record. The earlier review material I used is my own role's round-10 record and harness scripts (re-used as round-11 copies, with only headers, ports, diff ranges and the findings list changed), the findings.json entries, D-055, and the orchestrator's Node 24 audit log. I grant no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 is not engineering gate DG7.

checks_run.procedure: Confirm the frozen candidate. Check HEAD, that the repository is not shallow, and the recomputed candidate ID, both in the repository and in a full disposable clone checked out at the freeze commit 32e6478. Check that HEAD differs from the freeze commit only in candidate-excluded metadata, and that both fix commits are ancestors of the freeze commit.
checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG1; git clone . $TMPDIR/rev && git checkout 32e6478 && node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG1; git diff --stat 32e6478 HEAD; git merge-base --is-ancestor 7c3ebb2 32e6478; git merge-base --is-ancestor d54c151 32e6478
checks_run.environment: Linux sandbox, pnpm 10.33.0; repository /home/user/My-owns (HEAD d8eb695) and a full disposable clone under $TMPDIR (removed afterwards)
checks_run.expected: candidate_id sha256:e5cc6ef9…afeb8 (391 files) in every computation; HEAD..32e6478 limited to excluded metadata; the fix commits are ancestors
checks_run.actual: Both computations give sha256:e5cc6ef982ba7d53ed80138c0cbaa0119bcfe8dcaad4e324b5dafdb6431afeb8 (391 files). Neither tree is shallow. HEAD d8eb695 adds only the round-11 assignments, the candidate manifest and stages.json, all of which the candidate excludes. 7c3ebb2 (F-DG1-011) and d54c151 (F-DG1-214/132/215) are both ancestors of 32e6478.

':!docs/delivery/<metadata>'; git diff --stat 265af7e 32e6478 -- packages/ apps/api/src/modules apps/web/src docs/architecture docs/source; git diff 265af7e 32e6478 -- apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts | grep -v comments

checks_run.procedure: Verify F-DG1-011. Phrase-scan the D-055 row at 32e6478 for the removed overclaims and the required runtime statements. Read the member-audit sentence in full, and check that the evidence it cites exists in the candidate and that the claims match that evidence and my own re-run (checks 04-06).
checks_run.command: git show 32e6478:docs/delivery/decisions.md | grep '^| D-055' > d055.txt; grep -o -F <phrases> d055.txt | wc -l; git ls-tree 32e6478 docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/orchestrator/node24-member-audit.log; grep -n -i 'MEMBER AUDIT|v22|v24|exhaustive' architecture.testkit.ts
checks_run.expected: 'closes the whole' and 'prevents further' are gone. The default-deny claim is limited to module imports and process members, and the member-enumeration reach is named as residual (a). The audit runtime (Node 22.22.2) and the Node 24.21.0 re-audit are named, with evidence that exists. Any remaining 'exhaustive' is only a quote of the superseded D-053/D-054 framing.
checks_run.actual: 'closes the whole' = 0 and 'prevents further' = 0. The row now says the default-deny 'structurally closes the module-IMPORT and process-MEMBER loader/exec classes version-independently'. It says this does NOT cover a native-loader MEMBER of an allow-listed module (F-DG1-130) nor its runtime-enumeration reach (F-DG1-132/215, residual (a)), and that 'default-deny is not a claim that no further adjacent route exists'. The audit is 'performed on Node v22.22.2 (the build-sandbox floor) and re-run … on Node v24.21.0 (the production target, ADR-0001)'. The cited log is committed in the candidate. Both remaining 'exhaustive' hits are quotes of the superseded D-053/D-054 framing. The claims match my own evidence. On the member scan, setEngine is the only loader member on both runtimes (check 05). On process members, every spelled, aliased, destructured and enumerated form is flagged (check 06). On lint behaviour, 109/109 on both runtimes (check 04). The F-DG1-010/011 pattern of a version-detached claim is resolved, not repeated. Observation only, not a finding: the Rationale/evidence column still cites the round-9 counts 101/101 and 294/294, which are decision-time evidence. F-DG1-011 listed that refresh as optional.

checks_run.procedure: Independently re-run my round-10 member-name scan of the 7 allow-listed built-ins, plus a presence check of the dangerous process members, on both Node 22.22.2 and Node 24.21.0. This tests the D-055 claim that the Node 24 re-audit gives an identical result.
checks_run.environment: repository read-only; node v22.22.2 (OpenSSL 3.5.5) and node v24.21.0 (OpenSSL 3.5.8)
checks_run.expected: crypto.setEngine is the only loader member on both runtimes; any Node 24-only name match is benign; the process members listed in the orchestrator log are present on both
checks_run.actual: Both runtimes give the same name matches. The one exception is Node 24's util.convertProcessSignalToExitCode, a pure signal-to-exit-code mapping and not a loader, and Node 22's util.isNullOrUndefined. crypto.setEngine is the only native loader on both. os.constants.dlopen is a plain object of RTLD numbers. util.debug/debuglog are logging helpers. All 10 dangerous process members are present on both runtimes, and none is in SAFE_PROCESS_MEMBERS. This agrees with docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/orchestrator/node24-member-audit.log.

checks_run.procedure: Test D-055's revised wording that the default-deny 'structurally closes the module-IMPORT and process-MEMBER loader/exec classes'. My own probe (copied temporarily into the clone, then removed) feeds fileViolations() these forms: process.kill, destructuring, globalThis.process, a literal computed key, an alias, Reflect.get with a built key, Object.entries(process), node:child_process, dynamic import('node:vm') and node:module createRequire. It also feeds two allowed controls.
checks_run.command: cp 06-process-member-form-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom-r11-probe.test.ts; node vitest.mjs run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-dom-r11-probe.test.ts (node22, node24); rm the probe
checks_run.environment: disposable clone; node v22.22.2 and v24.21.0
checks_run.expected: Every process-member and module form gives at least 1 violation; process.env and node:crypto randomUUID give 0
checks_run.actual: P1-P7 and M1-M3 are all flagged, with 'process used as a value', 'computed member of process', 'globalThis.process', 'reflection via Reflect' and 'imports non-allow-listed node built-in'. OK1 process.env = 0 and OK2 randomUUID = 0. The results are identical on both runtimes (12/12). The process-member class is closed syntactically, including aliasing and enumeration, because process cannot be used as a value. The D-055 wording is accurate.

checks_run.environment: disposable clone; PostgreSQL 16.13 throwaway clusters under $TMPDIR (removed); node v22.22.2 / v24.21.0

summary: PASS with no new finding. F-DG1-011 is verified closed. D-055 drops 'closes the whole … class' and 'prevents further adjacent-route findings', limits the default-deny to module imports and process members, names the enumeration reach as residual (a), names the audit runtime Node 22.22.2, and records the Node 24.21.0 re-audit with committed evidence. My own scans on both runtimes agree: setEngine is the only loader member, and every process-member form is flagged. No regression: the round-11 product-tree change is the web test harness, test-only lint comments and self-checks, and decision text, with no product, contract, data or i18n change. On the frozen candidate sha256:e5cc6ef9…afeb8, on both Node 22.22.2 and Node 24.21.0: unit 302/302 (web 110/110 on Node 24; the negative control reproduces the 12 AbortSignal failures with built-in jsdom); architecture 109/109; integration 200/200 on each runtime. The live AR/EN scenario passes 108/108 on Node 24, covering closure 422/G6, scoped access, identity, cursor pagination, provisional branding and Unknown states. Static checks are clean, the register is unchanged and complete, and the prior domain closures hold.
